**Short answer:** for most flyers, get a power bank under 100 Wh. The Baseus Blade H1 is the best pick in the results I have, and the Baseus PicoGo AM52 is the better choice if you only need to charge an iPhone.

## Picks

**Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W), $89.99: best for most people**
- It's about 74 Wh, under the 100 Wh limit, so it's carry-on legal.
- It can charge a laptop and a phone. It has 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports and supports pass-through charging.
- It weighs about 451 g (the page also says 1.08 lb, about 490 g).
- No working discount code was found as of 2026-10-24.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah

**Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10,000 mAh, 45 W), $53.99 with code AM52: best for iPhone-only users**
- It's about 37 Wh, so it's carry-on legal.
- It charges wirelessly and magnetically at 25 W on iPhone 16 and 17 (not the 16e). iPhone 12 to 15 get 15 W.
- It puts out 45 W over USB-C. It's $59.99 without the code, which was last tested 2026-10-24.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w

Both buy links are affiliate links, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you. These two products are also the only ones in my search results, and both are from one brand. This isn't a broad comparison of every power bank, but both fit the airline rules below.

## Rules to know
- **Carry-on only.** Power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Under 100 Wh.** Banks of 101–160 Wh need airline approval, with a maximum of two. Anything over 160 Wh is not allowed ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Protect the terminals.** Use the original packaging, tape, or a pouch. Don't bring damaged or recalled batteries ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Airlines can be stricter.** Southwest, for example, has limited each customer to one power bank since April 20, 2026. It must stay out of the overhead bin, can't be charged from in-seat power, and must be visible while in use ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)). Check your airline's policy before you fly ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).

If you tell me your phone and whether you'll charge a laptop, I can narrow it down.
